decisions.reason: Proof 2.1 incorrectly asserted domain-restriction equivalence for arbitrary extended-real saddle functions. For X={0}, Y={0,1}, Psi(0,0)=0 and Psi(0,1)=+infinity, restriction to the finite domain creates a saddle while the original left inequality fails. Replaced only the proof claim by the exact omitted-slice conditions; the Definition is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Confirmed missing executable input/call semantics: the old text required exact solves and finite caps without naming routines, checker inputs, a budget rule or a precise exhaustion branch. Added supplied deterministic solver/checker programs, sound exact-minimizer certificate postconditions, shared per-block step caps with last-step success precedence, sequential tentative updates, atomic commit and explicit failure/exhaustion outputs. Exact Gauss-Seidel block equations and all admitted problems are retained; nonattainment cannot yield success.

Confirmed that the old capped wrapper omitted executable solver/checker inputs and an unambiguous budget/status rule. Added supplied deterministic programs with sound certificates for exact attained minimum-norm minimizers, explicit ordered calls, total per-block step caps and atomic state commit. Made exact-recurrence attainment conditional. For f(x)=-x and K=0, no finite point minimizes the x objective, so no sound checker can certify success; failure/exhaustion now returns the old state rather than requiring a nonexistent minimizer. The recurrence, residual/dual outputs and minimum-norm tie-break are preserved.

False positive: def-proper-closed-convex-function-on-rn defines properness (nonempty finite domain), convexity (with the 0*infinity endpoint convention) and closedness separately. The subdifferential Definition explicitly assumes only proper and convex; its reference to that convention does not impose closedness. The lemma has exactly that extended-real codomain and those assumptions. Its supremum proof excludes minus-infinite conjugate values using a finite competitor, treats both infinite cases, and at finite values rearranges the maximizer inequality into the defining subgradient inequalities. No extra convention hypothesis or edit is needed.

Confirmed missing cap/program inputs and ambiguous finite failure branches. Added supplied deterministic proximal solver and sound certificate-checker programs, positive integer dual/primal caps, precise shared per-call step accounting, success-on-last-step precedence, ordered calls with an explicit failed-call field, and atomic state commit. The unique proximal points remain mathematically defined by the existing existence theorem; no generic finite evaluator is inferred from that theorem. Exact recurrence, domain restriction, extrapolation and strict norm bound are unchanged.
